quizzes.title: Beyond the Basics Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: More Collections, Generics, Lambdas & Streams, Files & I/O.

questions.prompt: Which collection does not allow duplicate elements?
questions.explanation: A Set stores each value only once. Adding a value that is already in a HashSet is ignored, while lists and deques keep duplicates.
A queue is first in, first out. poll() removes and returns the head ("first"), so one element is left.
filter keeps the numbers greater than 5 (12, 8, 20) and map doubles them, giving [24, 16, 40].

questions.prompt: Why do we write List<String> instead of a plain List?
options: To let the compiler check the element type and avoid casts
To make the code run faster
To allow a list to hold any mix of types
questions.explanation: Generics tell the compiler which type a collection holds, so mistakes are caught at compile time and you do not need to cast values when you read them.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of try-with-resources when working with files?
options: It creates the file if it is missing
It closes the resource automatically, even when an exception occurs
questions.explanation: A resource opened in the try brackets is closed automatically when the block ends, whether it finishes normally or throws an exception.

questions.prompt: Complete the stream method that counts the matching names.
questions.explanation: count() is a terminal operation that returns how many elements are left after the filter. Sara and Bilal have more than 3 letters, so it prints 2.
